Who Said What

The people, notes and papers behind Mom's care, in one place.

Download PDF

The admissions director's card is in your coat pocket, what your cousin said about Medicaid is in a text thread, and your notes from the call with the bank are on the back of an envelope.

This page doesn't ask you to weigh any of it. It asks who you've talked to, what each one told you and when, and who in the family has the note or the paper.

The people

One row for each person or place the family has heard from. Write the name beside the role. Leave the row empty if you haven't spoken to anyone in it.

What's missing, and who will ask for it

Any row above with an empty cell, and any document that still needs to be collected. Put a name next to each.

For example Nothing in writing from the call with the business office. Denise will ask for it by email. No date on the note from the bank; Marcus will check his phone log.

How to use it

  • Write what each person said as close to their own words as you can, and the date. If you can't remember when, write “not sure”.
  • Where two people told you different things, leave both rows as they are. Each difference is a question to bring to your Medicaid planner, not something to settle on this page.
  • Don't rewrite or summarize a document here. Just say where it is.
  • Bring this page and the papers to the planning conversation.

What this page doesn't do

It doesn't say which piece of advice is right, and it doesn't explain what any letter, notice or statement means. If you read something you don't understand, that's a question for the person who wrote it or for your Medicaid planner. Nothing here is legal, financial or tax advice.
